non_goals: V8 lite mode / jitless / heap-size clamps: hard constraint 2 — materially hurts JS speed; V8 defaults are PGO-tuned and stay untouched.

Windows working-set trimming (EmptyWorkingSet on freeze): no mechanism exists at this pin — WorkingSetTrimmer::GetInstance() returns a NoOp on non-ChromeOS (chrome/browser/performance_manager/mechanisms/working_set_trimmer.cc:32-39); building one is an invasive patch for a benefit Windows' own memory manager mostly provides.
Disabling the warm spare renderer (kSpareRendererForSitePerProcess, content_features.cc:1150): saves ~one idle renderer but slows every cross-site navigation — FAST pillar wins.

Shrinking Blink's strong memory cache (kMemoryCacheStrongReference, 200MB threshold on Windows, blink features.cc:1733-1751): deliberate memory-for-speed cache; cutting it degrades reload/back-nav; pressure-driven purge (MEM-04) already reclaims it when it matters.
Disabling BackupRefPtr/MiraclePtr to reclaim allocator overhead: SECURE pillar wins; cost documented instead (MEM-08).
--process-per-site as default: crash blast radius, poor discard granularity, and upstream's bounded same-site reuse already ships enabled — opt-in only (MEM-10).

V8 GC parameter fiddling (kV8MemoryReducer / kV8MemoryReducerDelay / kV8ScavengerHigherCapacity, gin/gin_features.cc:88-109): unmeasured speed-vs-memory effects, no upstream launch signal; not worth solo-maintainer benchmark burden.
Reducing back/forward cache entries: directly hurts back-navigation speed (FAST); bfcache pages already freeze and are purged/evicted under pressure.
Lowering the renderer process limit (--renderer-process-limit): degrades isolation and causes cross-site process sharing jank; the freeze/discard stack (MEM-01..05) is the correct pressure valve.
Brave-style fingerprint farbling and other large privacy patch series: out of scope per constraint 3 (rebase budget) and not a memory lever.

proposals.title: Memory Saver ON by default (medium aggressiveness)
proposals.change: Two-line stage-90 patch in RegisterLocalStatePrefs (components/performance_manager/user_tuning/prefs.cc:34-35): register kMemorySaverModeState default as MemorySaverModeState::kEnabled (2) instead of kDisabled (0). Leave kMemorySaverModeAggressiveness at its registered kMedium default (memory_saver_mode_policy.cc:201-224: discard after 4h backgrounded, max 15 revisits). Fold into patches/90-default-prefs-hardening.patch or a new 90-memory-defaults.patch.

This is Chrome's shipped, battle-tested Memory Saver; Google enables it for many users via Finch, which Slipstream never receives — so the code default is the only default. Migration code (prefs.cc:129-155) only overwrites the default when the user explicitly set the old pref, so the flip is safe. DiscardEligibilityPolicy protections (audio, form input, capture, exceptions list) all apply; discard ring treatment (kDiscardRingTreatmentEnabled, default true) makes discards visible.
proposals.risks: Discarded tabs reload on focus (state kept via session restore, but scroll/JS state loss possible on badly-behaved pages). Users can disable or add site exceptions at chrome://settings/performance. Registered-default flip means enterprise MemorySaverModeSavings policy still overrides cleanly.
proposals.cws_impact: None. No UA, extension pipeline, or webstorePrivate surface touched.
proposals.pillar_conflicts: None; supports FAST (fewer live renderers competing for CPU).

proposals.title: Enable freeze-on-memory-pressure on Windows (kInfiniteTabsFreezingOnMemoryPressure)
proposals.change: Stage-90 patch: components/performance_manager/features.cc:235-236 — flip kInfiniteTabsFreezingOnMemoryPressure to enabled. Keep param defaults (5s check interval, freeze when available physical memory < 15%; features.cc:238-248).

Eligibility respects the full CannotFreezeReason set (cannot_freeze_reason.h:17-43: audible, WebRTC, USB/BT/HID/serial, capture, notification permission, weblocks, WebUI), so media/chat/dev workflows are protected.
proposals.risks: Freezing pauses pages that lack notification permission — a background web app polling without notifications may miss updates until refocused. Pressure-triggered only, so exposure is limited to low-memory situations where the alternative is discard or swap-thrash.
proposals.cws_impact: None. Extension pages/service workers are not tab PageNodes subject to this policy.
proposals.pillar_conflicts: None.

proposals.title: Enable renderer memory purge when pages freeze (kMemoryPurgeOnFreeze)
proposals.change: Stage-90 patch: third_party/blink/common/features.cc:1764-1770 — make kMemoryPurgeOnFreeze FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT on desktop (currently Android-only). Leave kMemoryPurgeOnFreezeLimit (features.cc:1772) alone.
proposals.benefit: When a page freezes (battery saver freezing, MEM-03 pressure freezing, bfcache), the renderer simulates critical memory pressure and drops V8 heap, Blink caches, and font/image caches (memory_purge_manager.cc:165-185). Ships enabled on Android, where memory purging is proven; on desktop only the 4-minute post-backgrounding purge runs today (kPurgeOnBackgroundingEnabled=true, memory_purge_manager.h:77-83). Makes every freeze event also a reclaim event — freezing alone stops growth but frees nothing.
proposals.risks: Very low: purge only fires on freeze, which only happens to protected-eligibility pages; a one-off CPU spike per freeze for the GC pass. Unfrozen pages rebuild caches lazily (slightly slower first interaction after long absence).
proposals.pillar_conflicts: Negligible FAST cost, paid only by frozen background tabs.

proposals.title: Enable infinite-tabs freezing (kInfiniteTabsFreezing) — v0.2 candidate behind soak gate
proposals.change: Stage-90 patch: components/performance_manager/features.cc:215 — flip kInfiniteTabsFreezing to enabled. Recommend landing DISABLED in v0.1, enabled in nightly, promoted to default at v0.2 after a soak period.
proposals.benefit: The 'infinite tabs' policy: all eligible tabs beyond the 5 most recent are frozen continuously, not just under pressure — CPU and memory growth stop scaling with tab count. Combined with MEM-04, hoarded background tabs settle to purged, frozen minima. This is the flagship differentiator for a memory-optimized fork: upstream has the entire mechanism at this pin but keeps it Finch-gated.

proposals.pillar_conflicts: Slight FAST tension: refocusing a long-frozen tab pays a wake-up cost (much smaller than a discard reload).

proposals.title: Stop pinning the default-search-engine renderer resident (kKeepDefaultSearchEngineRendererAlive off)

proposals.pillar_conflicts: Small FAST cost on first DSE navigation; MEMORY and baseline-RAM win.

proposals.title: Document --process-per-site as a power-user opt-in (not a default)
proposals.change: Ship a commented '# --process-per-site' example (with tradeoff note) in the default flags conf consumed by Thorium's kept windows-thorium-flags-conf.patch mechanism, plus an FAQ/DEBLOAT.md section. Do NOT make it default.

But upstream already ships the sane 80% of the win by default at this pin: kProcessPerSiteUpToMainFrameThreshold is FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT on desktop with a 2-main-frame threshold and 2GB per-process memory ceiling (content_features.cc:964-998). The distribution mechanism (Thorium's kept flags-conf patch) verified as available. Zero code, zero rebase cost, resolves a real design question with evidence. Keep.

non_goals: Canvas/WebGL/font/audio fingerprint farbling — Brave-scale renderer patch series; violates the solo-maintainer rebase budget (hard constraint 3). Rely on 3PC blocking + Privacy Sandbox off + uBO instead.

Referrer tightening beyond the platform default — strict-origin-when-cross-origin has been Chromium's default policy since M85; forcing kEnableReferrers=false breaks anti-hotlinking and some login CSRF checks for marginal entropy gain.

Disabling WebUSB/WebHID/WebSerial/Web Bluetooth — already user-gesture + per-device chooser gated (BLUETOOTH_SCANNING default ASK verified at content_settings_registry.cc:402); Slipstream's gamer audience actively uses WebHID/WebUSB configurators (VIA, Wootility, iCUE web).

Removing GCM/Web Push plumbing — the persistent Google connection is only established once a site holds a push subscription; ripping it out breaks a mainstream web feature for no default-state gain.

DNT + GPC enablement — VERIFIED ALREADY DONE at this pin: Thorium's thorium-browser-ui-default-prefs.patch flips kEnableDoNotTrack to true (visible in tree at chrome/browser/ui/browser_ui_prefs.cc:147-149) and GPC.patch ships Global Privacy Control; no new work, add both to the per-release verification checklist.

Intranet redirect random-hostname DNS probes — VERIFIED already off at this pin (components/omnibox/browser/intranet_redirector_state.cc:41-42 defaults to DISABLE_FEATURE); nothing to do.

proposals.title: Enable App-Bound Encryption: register the elevation service for Chromium-branded system installs
proposals.change: Three coordinated pieces. (1) Small patch to chrome/installer/setup/install_worker.cc: remove the #if BUILDFLAG(GOOGLE_CHROME_BRANDING) guards around AddElevationServiceWorkItems (definition at :117-139, call site at :365-372) so system-level installs register the service — uninstall.cc:639-647 already deletes it unguarded, and elevation_service.exe is already built (chrome/BUILD.gn data_deps) and packaged (chrome.release:120). (2) Wire Slipstream's reserved GUIDs from branding/brand.json (elevator_clsid {A3886921-...}, elevator_iid {0725683C-...}) into chrome/install_static/chromium_install_modes.h (currently still Chromium/Thorium's stock D133B120-.../bb19a0e5-... at :64-73 — shipping those would collide with a side-by-side vanilla Chromium). (3) Ship a system-level (--system-level) installer as the recommended default. ABE then activates automatically: browser_process_impl.cc:1556-1568 registers AppBoundEncryptionProviderWin at precedence 15 over DPAPI's 10 unconditionally on Windows. ANSWERS: ABE works fine in a rebranded fork with fresh CLSIDs — nothing is Google-keyed; caller validation (caller_validation.cc MaybeTrimProcessPath) validates the calling exe's install path dynamically, not a hardcoded brand. If the elevation service is NOT registered (per-user install, or installer skipped it): GetAppBoundEncryptionSupportLevel returns kNotSystemLevel for per-user (app_bound_encryption_win.cc:71-73) or CoCreateInstance(GetElevatorClsid()) fails REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG (:180-182) — the provider reports kPermanentlyUnavailable and OSCryptAsync silently falls back to DPAPI ('v10' data): no data loss, no user-visible error, just no ABE hardening. SMOKE TEST: (a) after system install, `sc qc SlipstreamElevationService` (GetElevationServiceName = base app name + 'ElevationService', install_util.cc:357-361) shows SERVICE_DEMAND_START; (b) HKLM\Software\Classes\CLSID\{A3886921-7254-47BC-97E7-28EE702B950B}\LocalServer32 points at elevation_service.exe; (c) after first run, Local State contains "os_crypt":{"app_bound_encrypted_key":"..."} whose base64 decodes to an 'APPB'-prefixed blob (app_bound_encryption_provider_win.h:41-46); (d) chrome://histograms shows OSCrypt.AppBoundProvider.Encrypt.ResultCode == 0 and, on second launch, KeyRetrieval.Status == success; (e) new cookie DB values carry the 'v20' prefix (v10 = DPAPI fallback); (f) negative test: per-user install must still work end-to-end with v10 data.
proposals.benefit: Infostealer resistance parity with Google Chrome: the OSCrypt key is decryptable only via a SYSTEM COM service that path-validates the caller, so user-context malware can no longer trivially DPAPI-decrypt cookies/passwords. This is the highest-value Windows security feature currently dead in every Chromium-branded fork.
proposals.risks: Installer patch is small but touches update/uninstall flows — must test install/upgrade/uninstall cycles. Portable-zip users and per-user installs silently stay on DPAPI (document in SECURITY.md; interacts sanely with Thorium's kept --disable-encryption portable switches since portable mode is never a system install). Moving/renaming the install dir breaks decrypt until re-encrypt (upstream handles via kRegenerateKeyForCatastrophicFailures, provider_win.cc:37-57). User-data-dir relocation via --user-data-dir gets kNotUsingDefaultUserDataDir = temporary unavailable (no data loss, provider_win.cc:194-202).
proposals.pillar_conflicts: None. One extra demand-start service; zero runtime cost until an encrypt/decrypt call.
